title: MemoryStand — presenter cut
presenterDisclosure: Presenter synthesised from the author's own photograph.
_notes: MEASURED CONSTRAINTS of grok image_to_video, established before building on them:
- duration accepts 6 or 10 ONLY. Asking for 15 returns '`duration` must be either 6 or
10 seconds. Got 15.' and generates nothing.
- 10s is chosen over 6s for PACE, not length. The generator fits the line it is given into
the clip it is given: the 6s cut delivered 3.3-4.7 words/sec, which sounds hurried
because it is. At 10s a 20-word line lands in 8.54s -- 2.34 words/sec. So every shot is
written to 17-24 words, and make_clips.py warns when a line falls outside that.
- shots after the first in a beat are seeded from the previous shot's LAST FRAME, so a beat
plays as one unbroken take instead of a jump cut on identical framing.
- it generates AUDIO as well as video, and if you do not give it words IT INVENTS THEM. An
early motion-only prompt came back saying 'So, to summarize the key findings from our
analysis, we can conclude that the results are promising' -- filler nobody wrote. So every
shot passes its exact line, and make_clips.py TRANSCRIBES the result and fails on drift.
WHAT THE SECOND VERSION FIXED. The first cut carried two false claims:
- 'six hundred poisoned claims, plus honest ones as a control' overcounted by 60. The five
attack classes sum to 540 (60+60+60+300+60); the 600 in poisoning.md's own heading
ALREADY includes the 60 control_honest cases. 540 attacks + 60 controls = 600 total.
- a panel read 'reasoning_source: fallback_memory, model_calls: 0'. Live /decide returns
anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5 with model_calls: 1 and has since the standby provider was
wired. The zero-model-calls claim is true of the PROMOTION path, which is a different
path, and beat 07 now says exactly that instead of blurring them.
It also never once said 'CockroachDB', while the contest requires the video demonstrate the
CockroachDB memory layer at work. Beats 03, 04 and 06 exist to fix that.
Every number spoken is traceable:

ADVERSARIAL PASS. 24 refuters over 8 beats x 3 lenses raised 7 disputes; an adjudicator that re-checked each against the repo upheld 2 and rejected 5. Upheld: 'refuses every honest claim' implied the judge arm saw all 60 controls when poisoning.md:65 shows n=6; and calling the two-candidate recall 'live' when the panel itself labels it a recorded run and today's live /decide returns five memories tied at distance 0.547. Rejected, correctly: 01-claim restates README.md:3's own headline thesis with the caveats on the panel beside it, and 04-admission matches the capture artifact exactly -- capture_evidence.py:55-64 documents that reusing the seeded tenant is WHY the runbook and Slack values come back held against a leftover human 500.

lines: Mem0 — an LLM picks ADD/UPDATE/DELETE. No confidence score at all.
Zep — an LLM sets validity windows. "Model-inferred, not authoritative."
AWS AgentCore — extraction and consolidation are LLM prompts. No verification API.
panelData.footnote: Each line cites the vendor's own docs or issue tracker. See README.

shots: Every shipping agent-memory system asks a language model whether its own memory is true. Mem0, Zep, AWS AgentCore.

panelData.headline: Nobody lied. The memory is still false.
panelData.body: And it will be handed to an agent at the next incident. That is how a memory store fills with true-sounding operational folklore.

shots: The failure isn't fraud. It's an engineer at two in the morning who restarts a service and watches the page clear.
They report in good faith that the restart fixed it, when the metric never moved. Nobody lied. The memory is false.

panelData.note: Admission is checked inside the vector search. Trust tier comes back as a column and is ranked afterwards, in code.

shots: That memory lives in CockroachDB. Every row keeps its embedding in a native vector column, beside the ordinary relational fields.
The vector index is prefixed by tenant and admission verdict, so one statement filters and ranks by cosine distance.

shots: Writing a memory is not automatic. Every claim is admitted or held, and the reason is stored beside it.
Slack says three hundred. The runbook says eight hundred. Both contradict a human-confirmed five hundred, so both are held.

panelData.footnote: 540 attacks + 60 honest controls · poisoning.md:14-19, 31-47 · judge arm n=6/class

shots: We measured it. Five hundred forty poisoned attempts across five attack types, plus sixty honest controls to catch false refusals.
Trust the caller and every attack reaches verified. Use an LLM judge, and it refuses all six honest claims it actually tested.
Only the outcome gate tells them apart, because it does not ask a model. It re-queries CloudWatch itself.
Claimed minus fourteen thousand two hundred. CloudWatch said minus fourteen thousand two hundred and five. Confirmed. Claim minus ten, refused.
